questions.question_text: An investor deposits $\$600$ at the end of each year for $10\text{ years}$ into an account earning $5\%$ p.a. compounded annually. Which geometric series represents the future value $FV$?

options.why: Treated as start-of-period payments (annuity due) rather than end-of-period payments.
Included 11 payments instead of 10 payments for a 10-year term.
Calculated compound interest on a single deposit rather than an annuity series.

questions.solution_text:
For end-of-year deposits, the first deposit compounds for $9$ years and the 10th deposit earns no interest.
$FV = 600 + 600(1.05) + 600(1.05)^{2} + \dots + 600(1.05)^{9}$

questions.question_text: A sum of $\$2000$ is invested at the end of each year for $14\text{ years}$ at $6\%$ p.a. compounded annually. Calculate the future value of the annuity.

options.why: Multiplied by $(1+r)$ as if payments were made at the start of each year.
Summed the payments without adding any compound interest.
Calculated compound interest on a single lump sum of $\$20\,000$.

questions.question_text: Sarah deposits $\$250$ at the end of each month into an annuity paying $7.2\%$ p.a. compounded monthly. What is the value of the investment after $4\text{ years}$?

options.why: Used the annual interest rate of $7.2\%$ instead of the monthly rate of $0.6\%$.
Multiplied by $1.006$ for start-of-month payments instead of end-of-month payments.
Calculated simple principal total ($48 \times 250$) without compound interest.

questions.question_text: A council deposits $\$1200$ at the end of each quarter into a park upgrade fund paying $4.8\%$ p.a. compounded quarterly. Find the amount in the fund after $5\text{ years}$.

options.why: Treated the annuity as an annuity due by including an extra factor of $1.012$.
Ignored compound interest and simply calculated $20 \times 1200$.
Used $n = 5$ years instead of $n = 20$ quarterly compounding periods.

questions.question_text: Marcus deposits $\$1500$ at the end of each year for $8\text{ years}$ into a savings bond earning $6.5\%$ p.a. compounded annually. How much interest did the investment earn?

options.why: Reported the total future value rather than subtracting total contributions.
Calculated simple interest on the total contributions ($12000 \times 0.065 \times 5$).
Subtracted $9$ contributions instead of $8$ contributions from the future value.

questions.question_text: An apprentice deposits $\$400$ at the end of each month for $3\text{ years}$ into a high-interest account earning $8.4\%$ p.a. compounded monthly. Find the total interest earned over the $3\text{ years}$.

options.why: Stated the future value instead of subtracting the total deposits made.
Reported the total contributions made without calculating interest.
Calculated interest assuming deposits were made at the start of each month.

questions.question_text: A medical clinic deposits $\$5000$ at the end of each year for $12\text{ years}$ into an account earning $7.5\%$ p.a. compounded annually. What percentage of the final accumulated balance comes from earned interest? Round to the nearest whole percentage.

options.why: Calculated the proportion of the balance from principal contributions rather than interest.
Divided the earned interest by the total contributions instead of the future value.
Calculated interest using simple interest rather than compound geometric series.

questions.question_text: An investor makes $20$ annual contributions of $\$3000$ at the end of each year at $8\%$ p.a. compounded annually. By how much does the compound value of the very first deposit exceed the compound value of the 10th deposit at maturity?

options.why: Subtracted the uncompounded $\$3000$ payment instead of the 10th deposit's future value.
Calculated the future value of the first deposit alone without subtracting the 10th deposit.
Used simple interest differences over 9 years.
